gap: No result ChatGPT got works out how many days of 24/7 footage each box can hold for four Reolink cameras at Reolink's own default bitrate (6,144 kbps on the RLC-810A, so 265 GB a day). The Reolink RLN8-410 maxes out at about 22.6–30.1 days on its internal drive, because Reolink's two pages give different drive limits (6 TB or 8 TB). The Synology DS225+ holds about 75 days with two mirrored 20 TB drives.
standout_why: I compared the pages ChatGPT cited and that I opened: Reolink's RLN8-410 product page and NVR store page, Synology's Device License Pack page and QNAP's QVR FAQ. ChatGPT's retention tables use a guessed 6 Mbps. None of them works from a Reolink camera's own default bitrate, and none caps retention at each box's largest supported drive. Reolink's product page says 'Up to 16TB (max. 8TB capacity for each HDD)', but its own RLN8-410 FAQ says 'Max. 12TB in total: Max. 6TB via SATA, Max. 6TB via eSATA', and no rival points out the conflict. One ChatGPT answer only hedges with 'subject to your hardware version's drive limits'. I did not open the reolink.com Synology buying guide (the top result).
decides: This confirms the split on the page. If the shopper wants a month or more of 24/7 footage from four 4K cameras without plugging in an external eSATA drive, the RLN8-410 falls short on some hardware versions (22.6 days on a 6 TB drive) and only just reaches it on others (30.1 days on 8 TB). A two-bay NAS with mirrored drives clears it easily (about 75 days on 2×20 TB). The NVR is still the simple pick for about 3 weeks of footage. For a month or more, the NAS wins. On licences for four cameras: Synology needs 2 paid licences, QNAP's QVR Surveillance needs 0 (8 free channels), the RLN8-410 needs 0, and UGREEN publishes no camera fee.

findings.label: Reolink 4K PoE camera default main-stream bitrate
findings.note: Quoted text: 'Mainstream: 4096Kbps - 8192Kbps (default: 6144Kbps)'. This is the input for every retention figure below.

findings.label: Storage used per day, four cameras recording 24/7
findings.note: 6.144 Mb/s × 86,400 s ÷ 8 = 66,355 MB per camera per day; × 4 cameras = 265.4 GB/day (decimal units, no filesystem overhead).

findings.label: Storage limit as stated on the product page
findings.value: Up to 16 TB (max 8 TB per HDD; 8 TB SATA + 8 TB eSATA); ships with a 2 TB drive
findings.source_title: Reolink RLN8-410 | Reolink NVR for 24/7 Recording
findings.note: The US page https://reolink.com/us/product/rln8-410/ says the same: 'Up to 16TB (max. 8TB capacity for each HDD)'.

findings.label: Storage limit as stated in Reolink's FAQ (conflicts with the product page)
findings.value: Max 12 TB total: 6 TB via SATA + 6 TB via eSATA; max 8 camera channels, and a dual-lens camera uses 2
findings.note: This is Reolink's own support article. Probably a difference between hardware versions; the page does not say which.

findings.label: Retention with the included 2 TB drive, 4 cameras
findings.source_title: Reolink RLN8-410 | NVR for Up to 12 Cameras & 24/7 Recording

findings.label: Longest retention on the internal drive only, 4 cameras
findings.value: 22.6 days (6 TB limit in the FAQ) to 30.1 days (8 TB limit on the product page)
findings.note: 6,000 ÷ 265.4 = 22.6 days; 8,000 ÷ 265.4 = 30.1 days. Adding an eSATA drive raises the total to 45.2 days (12,000 ÷ 265.4) or 60.3 days (16,000 ÷ 265.4). No redundancy either way.

findings.note: This excludes the drive and the camera PoE load, so a yearly kWh figure would not compare fairly with the Synology access-mode number. I did not calculate one.

findings.label: Share of Surveillance Station capacity used by four 4K cameras
findings.value: 4 of 20 channels and 100 of 200 fps (50%) at 4K H.265
findings.note: Spec: 4K H.265 '20 channels, 200 FPS'. 4 cameras × 25 fps (Reolink default) = 100 fps, which is 100 ÷ 200 = 50%. Under H.264 the limit is 170 fps, so 100 ÷ 170 = 59%.

findings.label: Camera licences to buy for 4 cameras
findings.source_title: Surveillance Device License Pack | Synology Inc.
findings.note: Synology: 2 default licences on a NAS, 'default free licenses will never expire'; packs of 1, 4 or 8, 'valid for good once activated'. The page lists no price.

findings.note: 16.98 W (Access) × 8,760 h ÷ 1,000 = 148.7 kWh. 24/7 recording keeps the drives spinning, so the 6.08 W hibernation figure does not apply.
